result.summary:
PASS. Independently re-derived the verdict from the real diff (git diff main...feature/WF03-ISS0457-20260904 -- lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex), not from ELIXIR-DEV's or CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's summaries.

Verification run synchronously, foreground, this turn:
- `mix format --check-formatted` -- exit 0, no output (clean).
- `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -- exit 0, no warnings.
- `mix test test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs` -- real output quoted: `Running ExUnit with seed: 187193, max_cases: 32` / `Excluding tags: [:keycloak, :wasm_hang, :lua_wallclock_race]` / `Finished in 11.0 seconds` / `Result: 47 passed`. 47/47, 0 failures -- matches ELIXIR-DEV's reported count, independently confirmed rather than trusted.

Implementation vs. design section 2, verified via the actual diff hunk (lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex:562-579): ELIXIR-DEV picked shape (i) conditional-preservation, as claimed. Traced the logic by hand: `winner = if is_nil(best), do: {prefix_before_value, old_value_raw, after_value}, else: best` -- best is set exactly once, on the FIRST depth-1 "status" match, and every later match's candidate tuple is computed but discarded, exactly matching the design's stated behavior ('best is set exactly once -- on the FIRST depth-1 status match encountered ... and is never overwritten by any subsequent match'). `acc` still accumulates `prefix_before_value <> old_value_raw` unconditionally on the recursive call regardless of which branch `winner` took, satisfying the design's explicit 'acc must still include every byte scanned regardless of whether this particular match became the winner' requirement -- confirmed by reading the line, not assumed.

Re-derived (not inherited) that every design-required preserved property actually holds by reading the surrounding, untouched code directly: depth-tracking clauses (`scan_for_status/4` clauses at :531-537, matched on `{`/`[`/`}`/`]`) are outside the diff's hunk entirely. `consume_json_string/1` (string-escape handling) is called but not modified -- the diff only touches lines inside the already-dispatched depth-1-KEY-match branch. The `depth == 1 and key_follows?(after_string)` guard (:554, nested result.status immunity) is unchanged; the diff is entirely inside the `if Jason.decode!(string_raw) == "status"` branch that guard already gates. `splice_top_level_status/2`'s own body (:507-518), including its `{_consumed, nil}` raise clause (zero-match invariant), is untouched -- confirmed by re-reading it directly, not cited from the design.

Hand-traced the actual duplicate-key case the property is about (mix run couldn't boot the full app in this sandbox -- LETFLOW_SECRETS_MASTER_KEY missing outside test env -- so traced by hand against the code read directly, which is sufficient since the logic is a straight-line accumulator with no hidden state): for `{"status":"DONE","other":1,"status":"COMPLETE"}`, first match sets best to the DONE tuple (best was nil); second match computes its own candidate but `winner = best` keeps DONE; end-of-scan `best` is the DONE tuple, so `splice_top_level_status/2` edits DONE -> COMPLETED and leaves the second COMPLETE occurrence untouched -- the same occurrence Jason.decode!/1 resolves to (first-key-wins), closing the exact divergence ISS-0457 reported.

Scope check: `git diff main...feature/WF03-ISS0457-20260904 --name-only` lists exactly docs/issues/ISS-0457.yaml, handoffs/WF03-ISS0457-20260904/* (diagnosis artifacts + all step handoffs), handoffs/orchestrator.log, handoffs/registry.json, lib/letflow/design/iss0442-lint-handoffs-minimal-diff-autofix.md, lib/letflow/design/iss0457-splice-first-wins.md, and lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex. No file outside the authorized set (lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex, the two named design docs, handoffs/) was touched. No new function, no new module, no new abstraction (behaviour/macro/generic plumbing) introduced -- the change is a minimal, local accumulator-selection fix confined to the existing handle_string_token/5 clause, exactly matching the design's own framing of option (a) as the minimal-diff choice over (b)'s heavier detection machinery. No crutch pattern: this is plain functional Elixir (recursive scan with an accumulator), not a place where gen_statem/supervision applies -- this module is a Mix task, not an OTP process, so idiom questions 1 (gen_statem) and 2 (supervision) from the REVIEWER role file are not applicable to this diff. No type-safety gap worth filing: `best`'s type (`tuple() | nil`) is unchanged by this diff and was already reviewed under ISS-0442. Checked docs/anti-patterns.md (grepped for lint_handoffs/splice/scan_for_status/handle_string_token) -- existing entries about this module concern workflow usage of the lint tool (agents not running it before pushing), not scan_for_status/splice_top_level_status internals; nothing applicable to this specific diff.

Both corrected-text edits (design section 3.1 for lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex's comment, section 3.2 for lib/letflow/design/iss0442-lint-handoffs-minimal-diff-autofix.md's algorithm step 2) read directly in the diff and confirmed to match the design's verbatim text.

Verdict: PASS. No gaps found.
